title: Private Health Insurance Amendment (Modernising the Private Health Insurance Rebate) Bill 2026
short_title: Private Health Insurance Amendment (Modernising the Private Health Insurance Rebate) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would remove the higher private health insurance rebate for people aged 65 and over, applying the same rebate calculation across age groups.
Rebate eligibility and rates would depend on income alone, while the existing income tiers and annual indexation arrangements would continue under the revised calculation.
The changes would apply to premiums paid on or after 1 April 2027 for cover on or after that date, including rebates claimed through tax offsets.
changes: Separate references to the higher rebate percentages for older people would be removed from the income-tier provisions.
The concession preserving a departing older policyholder's higher rebate for remaining insured people would be repealed.
The associated exemption in the Age Discrimination Act 2004 would be removed.
summary.affected: Privately insured people aged 65 and over, others sharing affected policies and insurers are affected.

speeches.speaker: Mark Butler
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of a bill removing higher private health insurance rebates for people aged 65 and over from 1 April 2027 while retaining means testing and other supports. Argued the change would restore intergenerational equity and redirect an estimated $3 billion in savings to additional aged-care beds, packages, shorter waits and improved care.

speeches.speaker: Tony Sheldon
speeches.brief: Presented the Selection of Bills Committee's seventh report and moved its adoption; the report recommended immediate referral of four bills concerning defence, health insurance and tax reform to Senate committees with reporting dates from 13 August to 7 October 2026, while an amendment proposed referring a workplace relations bill by 10 August.
